response.query: What minimum independent-dates-per-horizon and age-precision thresholds should we adopt to robustly test whether the Europe–Asia chronological gap is real or artefactual?
response.answer: To robustly test the Europe–Asia chronological gap, adopt a minimum of 10 independent dates per horizon and an age-precision threshold of ±50 years.

After years of study, a test that measures aging is on the horizon. Posted October 4, 2019|Reviewed by Kaja Perina * : Share on BlueskyShare on Bluesky * Take our Positive Aging Test * Find a therapist specialized in aging concerns Forget the number on your cake, your true biological age can be gleaned from your DNA. For decades, biogerontologists have been on the hunt for a biomarker of aging—a single test that measures the biological process of aging and could even accurately predict your “biological age.” Unlike your chronological age, your biological age doesn’t just measure your time here on earth, but rather how your body functions relative to others of the same chronological age as you. But depending on your health and genetics, your biological age might be closer to that of someone who is 55 or 75. It turns out that one of the most interesting new biomarkers of aging is the genetic material, DNA. For one study, researchers measured telomere length in 143 people over age 60, and then followed subjects over more than a decade, and found that people with longer telomeres had lower mortality rates than those with shorter telomeres. Horvath was able to identify 350 CpG methylation sites, the level of methylation of which could closely predict chronological age in many different tissue types. The question is whether people identified as older or younger than their chronological age are actually biologically younger or older. * Take our Positive Aging Test * Find a therapist specialized in aging concerns The precision of the epigenetic clock greatly exceeds that of measuring telomere length.

Your chronological age is the amount of time that has passed from your birth to the given test date. It’s your age based on the calendar year and expressed in terms of years, months and days. While chronological age is the number of years a person has actually lived, biological age refers to how old a person appears to be. ## How to Calculate Chronological Age. Our Chronological Age Calculator finds your chronological age by subtracting your date of birth from the test date. The only difference is that when you subtract months, you only use numbers 1-12 and for days, you only use numbers 1-31. The person checked his chronological age on June 13, 2020. So the person’s chronological age is 24 years 8 months and 14 days. This very result we can instantly obtain using our Chronological Age Calculator without resorting to tedious manual calculations. Title: 'Men should date women half their age plus seven': The strange dating rule that dates back to 1901 | The Independent | The Independent
## Stay up to date with notifications from The Independent. # 'Men should date women half their age plus seven': The strange dating rule that dates back to 1901. ## Is age really just a number? Ever heard of the rule that men should date women who are half their age plus seven? It turns out to be relatively well established, dating back more than 100 years to a book by Max O’Rell written in 1901, and the 1951 play The Moon is Blue. But does it stand up to scrutiny, or is it just a baseless rule perpetuated by men who want to justify dating younger, and less mature, women? Relationship expert Susan Winter said, “I find it amusing that there’s an equation for the ‘optimal’ age gap in love. As for why she thinks the equation has endured for so long, Winter said, “There's no logical reason for this to be a ‘rule.’ Nor does this mathematical equation determine the 'optimal age gap.'”. Historically, a woman was to choose a man the same age, or five to 15 years older. For Russo, “It is more important to look at the life stage someone is in to see if your values are similar than to base your decision on chronological age.”. However, she “could see the rule working out much better for men than women,” because “chances are a 30-year-old man dating a 22-year-old woman would be a much better match than a 30-year-old woman and a 22-year-old guy, as men typically lag behind women in maturity and relationship ready-ness.”. As for the endurance of the rule, Russo thinks it may have something to do with men being attracted to younger women. She said, “one reason why this may have endured is because men are generally more attracted to younger women and would like a rule that makes them feel it is acceptable to date younger.” So basically men are to blame. Try it at whatever age you like, and you will find it works very well, taking for granted all the while that, after all, a man as well as a woman is the age that he looks and feels.”.
